content: The treatment of Kala Azar (visceral leishmaniasis) in HIV-positive patients in India was investigated in a randomized clinical trial conducted in 2015. This trial compared the efficacy of AmBisome monotherapy with a combination therapy of AmBisome and miltefosine. The trial was registered under the ID CTRI/2015/05/005807, and the results were later published in 2019 in the journal Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (Volume 113, Supplement 1, Page S203). The study was led by Burza S, Pandey K, Mahajan R, Kazmi S, Alexander N, Lasry E, and others. In a separate study conducted in eastern India, Goswami RP and colleagues evaluated the protective efficacy of secondary prophylaxis against visceral leishmaniasis in HIV-coinfected patients over a 10-year period. This study was published in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in February 2017 (Volume 96, Issue 2, Pages 285-291). In Ethiopia, a prospective cohort study led by Diro E, Ritmeijer K, Boelaert M, Alves F, Mohammed R, Abongomera C, and others examined the use of pentamidine as secondary prophylaxis to prevent relapse of visceral leishmaniasis in HIV-infected patients. The study focused on the first 12 months of follow-up and was published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in October 2015 (Volume 9, Issue 10, Article e0004087). A subsequent study by the same group investigated long-term clinical outcomes in visceral leishmaniasis/HIV-coinfected patients during and after pentamidine secondary prophylaxis. This single-arm clinical trial was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2018 (Volume 66, Issue 3, Pages 444-451). Another Ethiopian study, published in February 2019 in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases (Volume 13, Issue 2, Article e0007132), explored the long-term outcomes and prognostic factors of visceral leishmaniasis in HIV-infected patients. This study, led by Diro E, Edwards T, Ritmeijer K, Fikre H, Abongomera C, Kibret A, Bardonneau C, Soipei P, Mutinda B, Omollo R, and van Griensven J, focused on the use of pentamidine as secondary prophylaxis based on CD4 levels. A systematic review by Alvar J, Aparicio P, Aseffa A, Den Boer M, Canavate C, Dedet JP, and others examined the relationship between leishmaniasis and AIDS over a 10-year period. This review was published in Clinical Microbiology Reviews in 2008 (Volume 21, Issue 2, Pages 334-359). The World Health Organization (WHO) has also provided extensive guidance on the control of leishmaniasis. A report from the WHO Expert Committee on the Control of Leishmaniases, held in Geneva in March 2010, was published as part of the WHO Technical Report Series (No. 949). The Cochrane Collaboration developed a tool for assessing the risk of bias in randomized trials, as described by Higgins JPT, Altman DG, Gøtzsche PC, Jüni P, Moher D, Oxman AD, and others in a 2011 article in BMJ (Volume 343, Article d5928). Similarly, Sterne JA, Hernán MA, Reeves BC, Savović J, Berkman ND, Viswanathan M, and others introduced the ROBINS-I tool for assessing bias in non-randomized studies of interventions, published in BMJ in 2016 (Volume 355, Article i4919). The GRADE Working Group has developed a handbook for grading the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations, updated in October 2013. This resource is widely used in evidence-based medicine. Finally, a systematic review by O'Neill J, Tabish H, Welch V, Petticrew M, Pottie K, Clarke M, and others emphasized the importance of applying an equity lens to health interventions. This review, published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2014 (Volume 67, Issue 1, Pages 56-64), highlighted the need to consider socially stratifying factors to address health inequities.
